title: Biloxi dances, early crowds and the hat-check income
summary: DeDroit describes his ten-man Biloxi band and how a drop in ticket price filled a dance.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, when did your- did you use a megaphone right from the first with your band, or when did that start?

Well, I first heard singing. When I had the Dixieland band, we didn't sing. But when I'd go to Biloxi, I'd bring ten men, see? Well, I'd bring ten men, and we'd play a few, you know, we had a big crystal ball, we'd put the lights out, that's all the entertainment we had. That's all the set you had. That's all we had. We didn't have any intermission. He didn't want any intermission, so instead of playing four hours, we played three. We didn't want any intermission. And we sent a couple of cases to post the dance down. And we were glad to get, you know, the one on the west. Sure. You see, because the New Orleans people used to go to Biloxi on the weekend, and they'd get out and everything. It wasn't the local people. Oh, I see. I found it out, because I went over there one week too soon, and I gave an answer, and I charged two and a half, and only had thirteen people. And a friend of mine said, Johnny, there's nobody in Biloxi. He's got two and a half dollars and a half. He said, because there's the local, the New Orleans people that support the thing. People from up in Birmingham, they come down, and people from New Orleans go over to the Gulf Coast. It was a different thing than it is now. So I gave another dance from that choice fifty cents, and I sold thirteen hundred tickets. I thought the fact there was Johnny D. Dwight in the recording orchestra, I could get, you know, make a lot of money. And this was a... Thirteen people. I said, what's... He said, Johnny, they don't have two and a half. So I got the sign, I changed it, two and a half to fifty cents. I made a hundred and ten dollars on the hats. Just on a hat check? Hats. Everybody wore hats and everything. This was what, about mid-twenties this was happening? I can tell you. It takes too much time. If I had known just what you wanted, I'd have to...
